title: The wrong process cannot make gold
odia: କୁହାଯାଉଥାଇ ସିନା, ତୁହାଇ ତୁହାଇ ପୁଟ ଦେଲେ କାହିଁ, ଲୁହା କି ହୋଇବ ସୁନା
literal_meaning: People may keep saying it, but will repeated firing turn iron into gold?
explanation: Repeating a process does not ensure the transformation wanted. This editorial reading questions an unsuitable method, not anyone’s capacity to learn.
meaning_odia: ଲୁହାକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ତତାଇଲେ ବି ସେ ସୁନା ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଏକା ଉପାୟକୁ ଦୋହରାଇବା ମାତ୍ରେ ଇଚ୍ଛାମତେ ଫଳ ମିଳିବ ବୋଲି ଭାବିବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ। କାମର ଉପାୟ ବଦଳାଇବା ଦରକାର କି ନାହିଁ, ସେଥିରେ ମନ ଦେବା ଉପଯୋଗୀ; ମଣିଷ ଶିଖିପାରେନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଏହାକୁ ଟାଣିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: Reformatting an inaccurate report cannot make its facts reliable. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: A metalworking image, not a claim of innate human rank or an instruction for processing metals.

title: Distance makes things look better
odia: ଦୂର ପର୍ବତ ସୁନ୍ଦର; ଦୂର ବନ୍ଧୁ ସୁନ୍ଦର
literal_meaning: A distant mountain is beautiful; a distant friend is beautiful.
explanation: Distance can hide the rough edges of a place or a relationship. What looks inviting from afar may feel different when we know its everyday difficulties. The saying gently questions an ideal picture; it does not claim that friendship needs distance.
meaning_odia: ଦୂରରୁ ପାହାଡ଼ର ଖାଲଢିପ ଦିଶେନାହିଁ; ଦୂରର ବନ୍ଧୁଙ୍କ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଅସୁବିଧା ବି ଆଖିରେ ପଡ଼େନାହିଁ। ନିକଟରୁ ଜାଣିଲେ ଯେଉଁ ତଫାତ ଦିଶେ, କଥାଟି ତାହାକୁ ମନେ ପକାଏ। ଦୂରର ସୁନ୍ଦର ଛବିକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା ଏହାର ଭାବ, ବନ୍ଧୁତା ଭଲ ରହିବା ପାଇଁ ଦୂରେଇ ରହିବା ଦରକାର ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: Someone envies a friend’s life from holiday photographs; a longer visit reveals ordinary chores and worries too. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The dictionary gives two parallel images: a mountain seen from afar and a friend kept at a distance. This explanation is an editorial reading of that contrast, not an origin story.

odia: ଏଡ଼େ ମଲାଠେଇଁ ଦିଓଳି ବି ତତଲା ଖିଆ!
title: Such poverty, yet hot food twice a day
literal_meaning: In such dire poverty, yet eating hot food at both meals!
explanation: The dictionary places this saying under extreme poverty. The line then sets that condition beside eating hot food at both meals: its surprise lies in the contrast. It can be read as a teasing challenge to a description of hardship, though the dictionary does not supply a separate use gloss. Cooking again costs fuel and work; a literary passage about one cooked-rice meal and one meal of pakhala helps explain the image. That context does not make hot food a reliable measure of anyone’s means.
meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏଠାରେ ‘ମଲା’ର ଅର୍ଥ ଅତି ଗରିବ ଅବସ୍ଥା। ଢଗଟି ସେହି ଦୁରବସ୍ଥା ସହ ଦିଓଳି ତତଲା ଖାଇବାକୁ ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ କରେ। ଦୁଇ ଓଳି ତତଲା ଖାଦ୍ୟର କଥା ଶୁଣି ଅଭାବର ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନାକୁ କଥକ ଥଟ୍ଟା କରୁଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗେ। ଏହି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ପାଠଟି ଶବ୍ଦର ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ରରୁ କରାଯାଇଛି; ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହାର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଅଲଗା କରି ବୁଝାଇନାହିଁ। କାହାର ଗରିବୀ ସତ କି ମିଛ, ଖାଦ୍ୟର ଉଷ୍ଣତା ଦେଖି ତାହା ସ୍ଥିର କରିହେବ ନାହିଁ।
english_summary: A contrast between described hardship and hot food at both meals; its teasing application remains an editorial reading.
odia_summary: ଦୁରବସ୍ଥାର କଥା ସହ ଦିଓଳି ତତଲା ଖାଇବାର ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ର।
usage_example: During an imagined discussion of household expenses, one person complains that nothing is affordable. A companion sees the freshly cooked evening meal and quips, “ଏଡ଼େ ମଲାଠେଇଁ ଦିଓଳି ବି ତତଲା ଖିଆ!” The reply comes back: “A hot meal does not tell you what we have had to go without.” (Original imagined use, not collected testimony.)
cultural_context: Recorded as ଢଗ under ମଲା, noun2, printed Praharaj page6322. Preserve the social sting rather than recasting it as a universal lesson about extravagance. The source establishes wording and the poverty sense; the teasing application is editorial. The separate Rudrakshya passage clarifies meal/fuel language but neither quotes nor explains this proverb. No first-use, popularity or community-wide endorsement is claimed.
